title: Orion Financial - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Initial discovery focused on Orion's network constraints and trust requirements for a Private/VPC deployment. Covered VPC peering vs Private Endpoints, CIDR overlaps, cross-region routing, audit/KMS requirements, and a proposed pilot plan for a single-region private deployment with a dedicated control plane.
topics: Private control plane and data egress
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-19
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sonia Patel (Orion Head of Platform), Ethan Ross (Orion Security), Lena Ortiz (Orion VP Product)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, I'm Maya AE on Redwood, with Diego our SE. Quick round intro?
[00:12] Sonia Patel: Sonia here, head of platform at Orion. We're looking at private deployments, mostly for regulated workloads, hi.
[00:17] Diego Alvarez: Hi Sonia, hi Ethan, quick agenda: networking, auth, compliance, and pilot scope.
[00:25] Ethan Ross: Quick note, security first — SOC 2 plus internal audit, we need KMS integration, and no public internet egress for inference traffic.
[00:34] Lena Ortiz: From product side we care about latency under 250 ms for small chat flows, and cost per 1k tokens is a factor.
[00:43] Maya Chen: Great — high level we offer Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Sounds like Private VPC is the main path, we support a private control plane and customer-managed VPC peering or private endpoints depending on your networking policy.
[00:58] Diego Alvarez: To dig in, two main patterns customers use: 1) VPC peering with our dedicated egress ENIs, or 2) Private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink style) to endpoint services. Peering is lower latency but requires non-overlapping CIDRs and route table work; endpoints can go through NLBs and are easier with overlapping ranges but add a tiny latency bump.
[01:22] Ethan Ross: Clarify — with peering, does traffic stay in our VPC or route through Redwood? We want no internet egress; all model tokens must be processed within our VPC boundaries.
[01:33] Diego Alvarez: Good question. With Private deployment we can run the runtime within your VPC (on-prem or VPC-hosted) so inference does not leave your network. With Redwood Private (hosted private model) we have a private control plane that you can isolate via PrivateLink and we deploy inference nodes into your AWS account — that keeps data in your VPC. If using Redwood Dedicated in our cloud, traffic is in our infra, but we support dedicated capacity and strict contractual protections.
[02:02] Sonia Patel: We're leaning toward a VPC-hosted deployment where Redwood's inference nodes run in our account. Our constraints: must use SAML SSO for admin, KMS for model keys, and audit logs forwarded to our Splunk instance. Also region constraint: we need everything in us-east-1 for data residency.
[02:20] Maya Chen: Perfectly common. We support KMS integrations and can push audit logs via CloudWatch or to an S3 bucket with lifecycle rules, and forward to Splunk. We'll capture the exact log schema later.
[02:35] Lena Ortiz: On region, if you run in us-east-1 can we get autoscaling across AZs there?
[02:40] Diego Alvarez: Yes — within a single region we deploy across multiple AZs for HA. Cross-region failover is supported but for your compliance you can keep everything pinned to us-east-1.
[02:51] Ethan Ross: CIDR-wise we have a large corporate CIDR, 10.0.0.0/8 split across teams. We do have smaller overlapping ranges with partners so peering could be messy.
[03:03] Diego Alvarez: If you have overlaps, PrivateLink endpoints are cleaner. Or we can propose a transit VPC/hub model. One caveat: PrivateLink endpoints require an NLB per endpoint and there is a per-GB charge, but it's usually minor versus engineering overhead of re-IPing.
[03:21] Sonia Patel: How about DNS? Do you expect changes to our route53 or will the endpoint be internal only?
[03:27] Maya Chen: We typically give a private DNS name that maps to the endpoint — you can keep it internal to Route53 private hosted zones. We'll coordinate on certs; we support mutual TLS if you need it.
[03:38] Ethan Ross: Key management — we need to wrap model keys in our KMS. Does Redwood key-wrap or do you require pluggable KMS?
[03:46] Diego Alvarez: We have two modes: customer-managed keys where the service is allowed to use a KMS CMK in your account (via IAM roles), or bring-your-own-HSM for extra regulation. For most enterprise customers we request a role with kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt permissions scoped to the CMK.
[04:02] Lena Ortiz: Any differences in latency between the modes?
[04:06] Diego Alvarez: Minimal; KMS calls are async for tokenization/initialization and cached. The runtime does not call KMS per token. The steady-state per-token latency is unchanged.
[04:16] Sonia Patel: What about model updates or versioning — we want to be able to pin versions and rollout via canary.
[04:23] Maya Chen: Redwood supports model pinning and canary rollouts in Private deployments. The control plane API (which can be private) runs rollouts and we can limit traffic for gradual shifts.
[04:33] Ethan Ross: Audit logs again — we need token-level audit for at least metadata (request id, timestamp, model version). Is that possible?
[04:41] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we emit token-level metadata and request traces. The full token text retention is policy-driven; by default in Private we can disable retention or keep it encrypted in your S3 for X days. We'll align retention to your legal requirements.
[04:57] Maya Chen: A couple of tradeoffs: fully on-prem/runtime in your VPC gives you max control but longer setup time; a private-hosted option (Redwood manages infra but isolated) is faster but requires trust in our private control plane. Which direction are you leaning?
[05:12] Lena Ortiz: We prefer us-east-1 VPC-hosted with Redwood-managed agents in our account. Essentially customer-owned VPC with Redwood AMIs or EKS configs.
[05:22] Sonia Patel: On networking, we need to ensure nothing routes outbound to the public internet except approved upgrades. How do we handle OS/package updates?
[05:30] Diego Alvarez: We support image-based deployments with the option to use your patch baseline and allowlist package sources via an internal NTP/proxy. We can also coordinate offline image delivery for air-gapped setups.
[05:44] Ethan Ross: Any default ports? We want to restrict egress.
[05:48] Diego Alvarez: The runtime needs outbound to your KMS and optionally S3 endpoints; we can use VPC endpoints (gateway or interface) for those. The control plane connectivity is via PrivateLink so minimal internet egress.
[06:01] Sonia Patel: Are there examples or reference architectures?
[06:04] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send a reference architecture doc and a sample CloudFormation/Terraform module. 
[06:10] Lena Ortiz: On capacity planning, our initial traffic: 300 concurrent users daily, peaks around 80 qps, mostly short prompts ~80 tokens. We want to start with a pilot for two models: an instruction-tuned chat model and an embeddings model.
[06:26] Diego Alvarez: For that profile, a small cluster with autoscale should cover you. We'll propose instance types — MPS/T4s or A10s depending on cost vs perf; we can run a benchmark.
[06:36] Ethan Ross: Benchmarks — we need p50/p95 latency numbers for our prompt mix. Can you run a perf test inside our VPC?
[06:43] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we typically run a bench harness in your account. We'll need IAM role and a small worker instance to drive load. We'll capture p50/p90/p99 and cost per token estimations.
[06:55] Maya Chen: Also worth calling out caching and KV prefix caching — for chat workloads we can reduce cost/latency by caching common prefixes. We'll include recommendations.
[07:06] Sonia Patel: Compliance — we require SOC2 + encryption at rest, SSO with SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and per-team quotas.
[07:14] Diego Alvarez: All supported. We integrate with IdPs via SAML/SCIM for SSO and user provisioning, and have RBAC and per-API-key quotas.
[07:23] Ethan Ross: Does the private control plane expose SAML endpoints? We want to host the IdP connection behind our IdP or allow SCIM push.
[07:31] Maya Chen: We configure SAML for the private control plane and can also offer SCIM for user sync. The endpoints can be internal-only via PrivateLink.
[07:40] Lena Ortiz: Pricing — can you ballpark Dedicated vs Private-hosted differences?
[07:45] Maya Chen: Very roughly: Dedicated reserved capacity is priced per-GPU hour + platform fee, good for predictable high throughput. Private/VPC deployment has a platform licensing component plus infra costs (your EC2/EKS). We'll send a tailored pricing sheet after we size the pilot.
[07:59] Sonia Patel: Any competitors we should evaluate? We're also looking at Anthropic, AWS Bedrock and a small self-hosted inference stack.
[08:08] Maya Chen: Noted. We often compare on latency/cost and ops overhead. We'll share benchmarks.
[08:15] Diego Alvarez: Quick note on multi-region: you said US-EAST only, but if you later want global failover we can replicate models to another region under your control. Cross-region replication requires additional encryption/key handling.
[08:30] Ethan Ross: Network ops question — do you require peering to a tiny Redwood overlay VPC or are we able to run everything in our account with only PrivateLink to control plane?
[08:39] Diego Alvarez: For the model runtime we can run entirely in your account. The control plane can talk via PrivateLink so no peering required. Some customers prefer peering for slightly lower latency between control and runtime but it's not mandatory.
[08:54] Lena Ortiz: Any SLA for Private deployments?
[08:57] Maya Chen: For Private deployments we offer an enterprise SLA that covers control plane availability if Redwood manages it; for customer-hosted runtime the SLA is on the platform features but infra uptime is customer-managed unless we provide ops runbooks or offer a managed service add-on.
[09:13] Sonia Patel: Can we get an SOC2 report and pen test history?
[09:16] Maya Chen: Absolutely — we'll share SOC 2 Type II and recent pen test summary in the next email.
[09:24] Ethan Ross: Ok, pilot scope and timeline?
[09:27] Maya Chen: Proposed pilot: 4-week technical pilot in us-east-1, run both models, include perf benchmark, security integration (SAML/KMS), and deliver audit logs to your S3 and Splunk.
[09:39] Lena Ortiz: That sounds good. Estimated start: 2 weeks after contract signing.
[09:44] Diego Alvarez: We'll need a small infra contact to provision roles and provide a dev VPC; we can provide TF templates.
[09:52] Sonia Patel: I'll assign someone. Also need to talk about onboarding support and escalation path.
[09:57] Maya Chen: We'll include an onboarding runbook, contact points, and 24/5 support for pilot.
[10:04] Ethan Ross: A few nitty-gritty items: IP allowlist for our security scanners, egress IP ranges for updates, and the exact log fields we will get.
[10:15] Diego Alvarez: We'll produce a network appendix with IP ranges (or note for PrivateLink there are no egress IPs), and the log schema.
[10:25] Maya Chen: Recap next steps: 1) Redwoods sends reference architecture & TF modules 2) Redwood sends SOC2 + security pack 3) Redwood proposes pilot pricing and sizing 4) Orion to provide infra contact, dev VPC CIDR, and timeline.
[10:42] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, we'll review and get back.
[10:46] Maya Chen: Great thanks everyone.

Notes / Links shared: Reference architecture: https://redwood.example.com/deck/orion-private-vpc (internal)
